notes: 3D-printed UIUC research propeller (Deters 2014). Blades are inserted in interchangeable hubs: three extra hubs change the blade angle by -10, -5 and +5 deg (Deters et al. 2014 Sec. III, Table 2), which is how the 'pitched' data sets were produced; their offset is the experiment's pitch_deg (nominal hub value). Geometry = UIUC 'tested' PropellerScanner geometry (both blades averaged) with the tip artefact corrected (see geometry.csv header); PropellerScanner may underestimate twist (Uhlig, cited by Deters et al. 2014), and the scanned twist is 1-2 deg above design over the outer blade, so geometry_design.csv (in extraction/) is a useful sensitivity check. Root: r/R 0.15-0.25 is the blade neck between hub block and blade (chord drops to c/R ~0.11-0.14); the solver blade starts at the first station (Rhub = 0.15 R). Blade material: 3D-printed plastic, flexible at higher rpm (Deters et al. 2014 say the 12 % airfoils were chosen to stiffen the blades). Polars: XFOIL Ncrit = 9 (tunnel Tu < 0.1 %); Ncrit = 5 alternative files are listed in each airfoil entry. Chord Re at 0.75R ranges ~24k-61k (c75 = 20.5 mm, 0.75*Omega*R at the lowest/highest tested rpm). Fluid: UIUC lab air assumed rho = 1.17 kg/m3, nu = 1.55e-5 m2/s (Urbana, ~225 m altitude, ~22 C; the database gives coefficients only).
